title: Validation of a paired input
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle $\mathcal O$, $r$ a register, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $c$ a machine configuration on input $x$. Assume the program's transitions at the specified states implement the prescribed validation procedure: the states $vU0,vU1,vS,vP1,vP2,vW0,vWF,vWT,rw_1,rw_2$ have the transition identities $hU0,hU1,hS,hP1,hP2,hW0,hWF,hWT,h_1,h_2$, respectively, and none of these states is an oracle-call state, as expressed by $cU0,cU1,cS,cP1,cP2,cW0,cWF,cWT,c_1,c_2$. Then, if $x$ is a valid paired encoding, the run from the configuration based on $c$ at state $vU0$, input-head position $1$, and register-head position $p$ reaches the corresponding configuration at state $next$, input-head position $1$, and register-head position $p$. If $x$ is not a valid paired encoding, that run instead halts with a rejecting output, preserving the indicated register-head positions and avoiding oracle-call states before halting.
hypotheses_covered: Specified transition identities hU0, hU1, hS, hP1, hP2, hW0, hWF, hWT, h₁, and h₂
No oracle calls at the specified states, as asserted by cU0, cU1, cS, cP1, cP2, cW0, cWF, cWT, c₁, and c₂
c is a configuration on input x
r is a register and p is an integer
